title: Onboarding drain must be daemon owned, not browser owned
summary: The slow onboarding UX came from POST /onboard/drain-queue owning a serial browser-triggered loop and using synchronous inject; sync inject deadlocked because the child called back into the daemon while the daemon waited. Onboarding drain now follows the judge-drain pattern: the route records queue metadata and wakes the daemon, while lib/headless-drain discovers bench/onboard queues, drains batches asynchronously, and live-injects when kept notes advance.
